Definition: of Chaldee origin corresponding to H4566 (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil:--Satan.
BiblicalUsage: Satanas is the devil himself, the accuser, and Paul names what is done with him. A man is delivered unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved; Hymenaeus and Alexander were delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme. And Satan hindered Paul himself, once and again, from coming to the Thessalonians.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Satan is real, personal, and limited: he hinders, he tempts, he accuses — and he is used by God to discipline His own. My position is that even being delivered to Satan is not abandonment, but a hard mercy aimed at saving the spirit.
